issues.t: CVT shudder, surging or transmission failure
issues.sym: The SUV shudders or surges when pulling away, the engine flares without the vehicle speeding up, a transmission warning light comes on, or it loses drive altogether.
issues.why: The continuously variable transmission (CVT) can let its steel belt slip under load. Metal dust from the slipping then contaminates the hydraulic valve body, and the problem gets worse. Mitsubishi issued service bulletin 20-23-001 telling dealers to replace the valve body or the whole CVT, and owners filed a class action over these transmissions.
issues.next: Have the CVT fluid and stored codes checked at the first shudder. Ask a dealer whether the bulletin and Mitsubishi’s 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty apply to your vehicle, which covers the original owner.

issues.t: Front crossmember rust lets control arm detach (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end over bumps, wandering steering, or in the worst case a front wheel that suddenly tucks in because the lower control arm has broken free.
issues.why: Road salt rots the front crossmember where the lower control arms bolt on. Recall 16V-458 covers 2003-2006 Outlanders and 2007-2013 V6 models, and recall 20V-279 covers 2008-2013 Outlanders, in salt-belt states.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer will inspect the crossmember and either seal it against rust or replace it free. If you hear clunks from the front, get it inspected before driving far.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure on early models
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, flaring revs between gears, or no drive at all, usually past 100,000 miles.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic in the first-generation Outlander wears out internally. RepairPal has more than 100 owner reports, averaging about 116,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or won’t engage, stop driving it hard and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuilt or used unit is the usual fix.

issues.t: Balance shaft belt failure
issues.sym: A rattle or slap from the front of the engine. If the belt breaks, the engine may run rough or suddenly die and refuse to restart.
issues.why: The 2.4L engine has a small belt that drives the balance shafts. Old or poor-quality belts can break, and the pieces can get caught in the timing belt and knock the timing out, which can damage the valves.
issues.next: Replace the balance shaft belt every time the timing belt is done, about every 60,000 miles, using a quality belt. If the engine dies suddenly, have it towed rather than cranking it repeatedly.

issues.t: Rear suspension clunks and uneven tire wear
issues.sym: Clunks or slapping noises from the rear over bumps, and choppy or uneven wear on the rear tires.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the rear lower control arms wear out, and the rear sway bar bushings and differential mounts can loosen. Often all three arms on a side need replacing, and rusted bolts may have to be cut out.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension inspected and get an alignment after any arm replacement so the new tires don’t wear out early.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leak and misfire
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the top of the engine, a burning oil smell, a check engine light or a rough-running misfire.
issues.why: The valve cover gasket hardens with age and leaks oil, including into the spark plug tubes, where it can short out the ignition and cause misfires.
issues.next: Replace the valve cover gasket and the spark plug tube seals, and clean any oil from the plug wells. Check the plugs and coils for oil damage.

issues.t: Temperature control knob hard to turn
issues.sym: The heater temperature knob gets stiff or sticks, making it hard to switch between hot and cold.
issues.why: The knob and the heater door linkage it moves stiffen up over time. RepairPal lists well over 100 owner reports on these years, and Mitsubishi has issued a service communication on it.
issues.next: Don’t force the knob or it may break. Have a shop check the knob and the linkage behind the dash and free up or replace the stuck part.

issues.t: Windshield wipers stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers slow down, stop partway, or quit completely, sometimes in the rain.
issues.why: Water can get into the wiper motor through its breather hole and corrode it (recall 17V-461). Separately, the ball joint on the wiper linkage can corrode and pop apart (recall 16V-791).
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; dealers replace the motor and repair the linkage free. If the wipers fail, pull over safely in bad weather.

issues.t: Accessory drive belt can come off (recall)
issues.sym: A squeal or slapping noise from the engine, then a battery warning light, heavy steering or an overheating gauge if the belt comes off. The engine may stall.
issues.why: The belt tensioner flange can crack (recall 18V-069), and engine pulleys can wear unevenly (recall 14V-562), letting the drive belt jump off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer replaces the tensioner, belt and worn pulleys free. If the battery light comes on while driving, pull over safely.

issues.t: Sunroof glass can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or rattling from the sunroof, or the glass panel lifting or coming off while driving.
issues.why: The sunroof glass can detach from its frame. Recall 18V-071 covers 2007-2010 Outlanders with a sunroof.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the glass assembly free.

issues.t: Brake lights do not come on (recall)
issues.sym: The brake lights stay dark when you press the pedal, and a cruise control or brake-related warning may act up.
issues.why: The brake light switch can malfunction. Recalls 08V-680 and 14V-564 cover 2007-2009 Outlanders.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights, and check your VIN for open recalls; dealers replace the switch free.

issues.t: Power steering pressure line leak (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid on the ground or engine, a whining pump, or steering that gets heavy.
issues.why: On V6 models with the 6-speed automatic, the power steering pressure line sits too close to other parts and can rub through and leak. Recall 14V-366 covers 2013 models and 2007-2012 models that got a replacement 6-speed transmission.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the pressure and return lines free. Leaking fluid near a hot exhaust is a fire risk, so don’t ignore it.

issues.t: Brake pedal hard at low speed (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels hard and the SUV takes longer to stop, mostly during slow driving.
issues.why: The check valve on the brake booster can stick closed, cutting the power assist (recall 09V-077).
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the check valve free.

issues.t: Corroded seat wiring connector can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from under the front seat area.
issues.why: Salty melt water can reach an unused power-seat wiring connector on the floor and corrode it, which can make it overheat (recall 08V-094).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer reroutes the harness above the carpet free. Keep floor mats dry in winter.

issues.t: Headlights, taillights or wipers act up (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights, taillights or wipers work erratically or stop working.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in the body control unit that runs these lights and the wipers can leave it with unstable voltage (recall 15V-232).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the control unit free.

issues.t: Heater blower motor stops working (recall)
issues.sym: No air from the vents, the fan only works on some speeds, or the windshield won’t defrost.
issues.why: The blower motor can fail. Recall 15V-233 covers certain 2009-2011 Outlanders built in specific date ranges.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If yours isn’t covered, have the blower resistor checked before replacing the motor.

issues.t: CVT whine or clicking from bad bearings
issues.sym: A whining, humming or clicking noise from under the vehicle that gets louder as speed goes up.
issues.why: Bearings on the pulley shafts inside the CVT can fail. Mitsubishi bulletin 15-23-003 tells dealers to take the CVT apart and replace the bearings and any damaged parts.
issues.next: Have a dealer check whether bulletin 15-23-003 applies; the repair falls under the 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty for original owners.

issues.t: Exhaust leak at the front pipe gasket
issues.sym: A louder exhaust, a ticking or puffing sound when cold, or an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The ceramic donut gasket between the exhaust manifold and the down pipe wears and leaks.
issues.next: Have the joint inspected and the gasket replaced along with new bolts and springs. Exhaust leaks near the cabin should not be ignored.

issues.t: CVT delays acceleration (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV hesitates or is slow to pick up speed when you press the gas, for example when pulling into traffic.
issues.why: The CVT control software could delay acceleration in certain conditions (recall 16V-563).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer reprograms the CVT computer free.

issues.t: Rear parking brake sticks or won’t hold (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake does not hold the SUV, or it drags and won’t fully release. You may smell hot brakes.
issues.why: Water gets into the rear calipers and rusts the parking brake shafts so they bind (recall 18V-070).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer repairs or replaces the rear caliper parts free.

issues.t: Second-row seat belt may not latch or hold (recall)
issues.sym: The right rear seat belt buckle cover comes off or the buckle won’t latch, especially after the seat backs have been folded.
issues.why: Folding the second-row seats can make the center buckle damage the right buckle (recall 20V-403, 2014-2019). Some 2019-2020 models also had that belt assembled wrong (recall 20V-280).
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; dealers modify or replace the belt parts free. Don’t seat a passenger there until it latches properly.

issues.t: Liftgate struts lose pressure (recall)
issues.sym: The liftgate won’t stay up on its own, drifts down, or drops suddenly.
issues.why: Rust can form on the liftgate gas struts and let them lose pressure or burst. Recall 25V-507 started in salt-belt states and recall 26V-252 expanded it nationwide.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces both struts free. Until then, don’t stand under an open liftgate.

issues.t: Liftgate struts on PHEV lose pressure (recall)
issues.sym: The plug-in hybrid’s liftgate won’t stay up, drifts down, or drops suddenly.
issues.why: The same rusting gas strut problem covered by recalls 25V-507 and 26V-252 also affects 2018-2022 Outlander PHEVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces both struts free. Don’t stand under an open liftgate in the meantime.

issues.t: Faulty relays can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls, loses power, or runs hot without warning.
issues.why: Some relays in the engine compartment were defective (recall 17V-609).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the relays free.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking software errors (recall)
issues.sym: Forward collision braking keeps braking after the danger has passed, or automatic braking, ABS, stability control or brake hold may not work, with warning lights on.
issues.why: Wrong software was loaded in the forward collision module (recall 18V-620) and the brake hydraulic unit on vehicles with adaptive cruise or an electric parking brake (recall 18V-621).
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; dealers update the software free.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid power reduced warning
issues.sym: A propulsion or "power reduced" warning comes on and the vehicle loses most of its power, sometimes at highway speed, or the gas engine won’t start to help.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the plug-in hybrid drive system that put it in a reduced-power mode. Dealers often can’t find a cause once the light clears.
issues.next: Get to a safe spot and have the hybrid system codes read right away, even if the light goes out. Write down when it happens so the dealer can match it to stored data, and keep repairs under warranty.

issues.t: Weak 12-volt battery causes random faults
issues.sym: The PHEV won’t power up, or several warning lights and electronic glitches appear at once.
issues.why: Besides the big drive battery, the plug-in Outlander has a small 12-volt battery that runs the computers. When it weakens, many systems act up.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery load-tested and replaced if it is weak before chasing other faults.

issues.t: Charging cable or plug overheating
issues.sym: The charging cord or plug gets very hot, smells burnt, shows melted plastic, or charging stops with an error.
issues.why: Owners have reported charging cords overheating at the plug, linked to a loose terminal or a damaged cable or outlet.
issues.next: Stop using a cable that is hot, cut or melted. Have the home outlet checked by an electrician and replace the cord.

issues.t: Backup camera freezes or goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera picture freezes, stays black, or doesn’t appear when you shift into reverse. The touchscreen may also lag or reboot.
issues.why: Software errors in the infotainment system stop the camera image from showing. Recall 25V-369 (which replaced 23V-345) covers 2022-2024 Outlanders and 2023-2025 PHEVs, and recall 26V-549 covers 2025-2026 Outlanders and 2026 PHEVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; dealers update the software free. Until then, check mirrors and turn your head when reversing.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or cranks but won’t start.
issues.why: The fuel pump wiring may have been fused incorrectly, which can make the pump fail (recall 22V-027).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the fuel pump free.

issues.t: Seat belts may not lock for child seats (recall)
issues.sym: The front passenger or second-row belt won’t stay locked to hold a child seat tightly.
issues.why: The automatic locking feature of the retractor can switch off before the belt is fully retracted (recalls 21V-596 and 22V-335).
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; dealers inspect and replace the belts free. Double-check that child seats are tight.

issues.t: Steering wheel control buttons stop working
issues.sym: The steering wheel buttons for the information display (tire pressure, oil life, menus) stop responding or come loose.
issues.why: Owners report the plastic button pad on the steering wheel failing or working loose.
issues.next: Have the dealer check whether the switch pad is still under the 5-year/60,000-mile basic warranty.

issues.t: Hesitation, loss of power or stalling
issues.sym: The SUV won’t accelerate when you press the pedal, jerks, shuts off while moving, or shows an engine malfunction warning that returns after being reset.
issues.why: Owners of newer Outlanders have filed NHTSA complaints describing these episodes; dealers often can’t reproduce them and no common cause has been confirmed.
issues.next: Have stored codes read as soon as it happens and keep records of every visit. Repeated unfixed stalling can qualify under state lemon laws.

issues.t: Adaptive cruise and collision warning drop out
issues.sym: Adaptive cruise control or forward collision warning shuts off with a radar message, slows hard for no reason, or is slow to resume.
issues.why: Owners report the radar-based driver aids disengaging or misreading traffic. Dirt, snow or a misaligned front sensor can also cause this.
issues.next: Keep the front radar area clean. If it keeps happening, have the dealer check sensor alignment and software, and report it to NHTSA.

issues.t: Seat belts slow to retract
issues.sym: The driver or passenger belt retracts slowly or not at all, and can get caught in the door.
issues.why: Owners report seat belt retractors that don’t pull the belt back in properly.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the retractor under warranty. A belt that hangs out can be damaged by the door.
